clue.text: Represent Foreign Office visiting a cold region briefly

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside a place, so one piece is put within another
made brief means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a country is a region; its last letter is cut
FO is the standard abbreviation for the Foreign Office

explanation.surface: A diplomat from the Foreign Office stands for their department on a trip to a chilly part of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: The Foreign Office slips into the shortened country, just before its final R; A and C go in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To account for something is to make it up or constitute it, as in 'women account for half the staff', a sense of represent.

clue.text: New pie chart’s inscription

indicators.note: something new has been remade, so the letters take a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
a graph is a chart

explanation.surface: A freshly drawn pie chart carries a caption or label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pie chart' reads as one familiar phrase, but the two words do separate jobs: one is shuffled, the other becomes its synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigraph is a carved legend on a building or statue, or a quotation heading a book chapter, so a kind of inscription.

clue.text: Glass maker is rejected by student arts venue

indicators.note: to reject is to throw back, so the word is turned round

blocks.note: taken as written
L for learner, a student driver's plate
the ICA is the Institute of Contemporary Arts in London

explanation.surface: A glassblower's work is turned down by a students' arts centre.
explanation.walkthrough: The ICA, the Institute of Contemporary Arts, is a gallery on the Mall in London. 'Glass maker' suggests a person, but it is the material.
explanation.definitionFit: Silica, silicon dioxide in the form of sand, is the main raw ingredient melted to produce ordinary glass.

clue.text: Pirate’s mistress, after removing old underwear, said ‘aye’ to get things going

indicators.note: something said is heard rather than read, so we want a word that sounds the same
removing means taking away, so a letter is dropped
getting things going means starting them, so this piece comes at the front of the next one

blocks.note: long johns are warm full-length underpants
aye and the letter I sound the same
a mistress is a lover; O for old is taken out
O is the abbreviation for old; this is what is removed

explanation.surface: A racy scene: the pirate's lover strips off their old underwear and says yes to start the fun.
explanation.walkthrough: Long johns plus I, then LOVER without its O, run together as LONG JOHN SILVER. 'Pirate’s' looks like a possessive, but the 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Long John Silver is the one-legged buccaneer in Robert Louis Stevenson's novel Treasure Island, the best-known fictional sea robber.

clue.text: Oddly the Arctic Circle in particular provides fuel

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside it
done oddly means done strangely, so the letters are put in an unusual order

blocks.note: taken as written
a circle is the shape of the letter O
anal means fussily particular, short for anal-retentive

explanation.surface: Strangely, the region round the North Pole is where we get our fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arctic Circle' reads as one place name, but the circle is O, sitting inside ANAL before everything is shuffled. Anal, for over-fussy, is informal.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthracite coal is the hard, nearly pure carbon form of coal, burned in stoves and furnaces for heat.

clue.text: Film companies – including Universal – eager to learn

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: film studios are movie production companies
U is the film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: Movie studios, Universal among them, are keen to pick up new skills.
explanation.walkthrough: Universal looks like the Hollywood studio of that name, which fits the film companies perfectly; here it is just the U film rating.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone studious devotes themselves to study and reading, keen to acquire knowledge.

clue.text: Turnover seen when Konsa goes up against Mo Salah

indicators.note: set right up against means butted together side by side, so two pieces join end to end

blocks.note: only the tail of the defender's surname, where it meets the next name
only the front of the forward's name, where it meets the previous one

explanation.surface: A football moment: Aston Villa's defender Ezri Konsa challenges Liverpool's Mo Salah and the ball changes hands.
explanation.walkthrough: Turnover sounds like losing possession in a match; it is a pastry. Write the two names hard up against each other, KonSA MO SAlah, and the answer straddles the join.
explanation.definitionFit: A samosa is a fried triangular pastry folded over a spiced filling, which makes it a savoury turnover.

clue.text: Side swapping ends makes game?

indicators.note: trading the two ends means the first and last letters change places

blocks.note: a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: In football the sides change ends at half-time, which is part of how a match works.
explanation.walkthrough: Game looks like a sporting contest, fitting the side and the switching of ends; it is wild animals hunted for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Game is the flesh of hunted wild animals and birds such as venison or pheasant, eaten as food.

clue.text: Sign of top hat scratching head

indicators.note: scratching out the head means striking off the first letter

blocks.note: a cap is a top or lid
a tricorn is a three-cornered hat, here without its first letter

explanation.surface: A man in a top hat scratches his head, a gesture showing he is puzzled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top hat' wants to be one thing, the tall formal hat; it splits into a lid and a three-cornered hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Capricorn, the goat, is the tenth astrological sign of the zodiac, covering late December to mid January.

clue.text: Job swap

blocks.note: first meaning: an occupation or line of work
second meaning: to exchange one thing for another

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase it suggests changing careers; the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a skilled occupation such as plumbing and the act of exchanging goods.

clue.text: Happening as drums extremely deficient before Ringo’s discovered

indicators.note: lacking at the extremes means missing both end letters
dis-covered means with the cover taken off, so the outer letters go

blocks.note: bongos are small hand drums; first and last letters go
Ringo with its outer letters stripped

explanation.surface: Ringo Starr, the Beatles drummer, is caught out when his drum kit is badly lacking.
explanation.walkthrough: Ringo invites a drumming connection, but he gives only his middle letters; the drums are bongos with both ends trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ongoing is in progress and continuing at the present time, so it is currently taking place.

clue.text: Skin on show in retreat

blocks.note: a hide is an animal's skin
out means visible, on display

explanation.surface: Bare skin on display at a quiet getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: Retreat looks like a verb for backing away; it is a noun, a place to go.
explanation.definitionFit: A hideout is a secluded shelter where someone can withdraw from view, which is one sense of a retreat.

clue.text: Nomad found in area between two large US cities

indicators.note: whatever lies between things is flanked on each side, so it sits inside them

blocks.note: NY is New York and LA is Los Angeles
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A wanderer turns up somewhere in the stretch of America between two big cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two large US cities' are the two usual abbreviations, New York and Los Angeles; A for area sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A nyala is a southern African antelope that ranges over woodland browsing for food, so a loose example of a roaming creature.

clue.text: Rivers maybe on flood alert – Red Cross initially delivering heroic sort

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of each word counts

blocks.note: Joan Rivers was an American comedian; 'maybe' flags her as an example
the first letters of these five words

explanation.surface: With rivers about to burst their banks, the Red Cross arrives to help, a brave rescue.
explanation.walkthrough: Rivers suggests flowing water, matching the flood; it is the comedian Joan Rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Joan of Arc, the French peasant girl who led armies against the English, is a famous example of a heroine.

clue.text: See 4
School governors organised clubs in church – with small sanctions

indicators.note: being in something means being inside it, so one part is placed within

blocks.note: C is clubs, the card suit
an LEA is a Local Education Authority, which ran state schools in Britain
to run something is to organise it
CE is the Church of England
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A school's governing body set up clubs at the local church, backed by minor penalties.
explanation.walkthrough: Sanctions looks like punishments, fitting the school setting, but it means permissions. LEA, a Local Education Authority, ran British state schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearances are official permissions or go-aheads, and sanction in its approving sense means exactly that kind of authorisation.

clue.text: Nice flat here has strange way to tell temperature

indicators.note: something strange is unusual or odd, so these letters come out in an unusual order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An apartment in Nice, on the French Riviera, has an odd way of measuring how hot it is.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice looks like the adjective, but it is the French city, which makes the old non-metric thermometer feel strange there.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fahrenheit scale, with water freezing at 32 degrees, is a system for measuring how hot or cold something is.

clue.text: Perhaps Albert Finney’s content with set I redesigned

indicators.note: the content of something is what is inside it, so the interior letters are kept
redesigning means laying out again, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: Finney without its first and last letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: The actor Albert Finney is happy with a stage set that has been rebuilt.
explanation.walkthrough: Albert Finney reads as one actor's name; Albert is split off as the definition, a first name whose famous surname is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein, the physicist of relativity, is one well-known Albert, so the surname is defined by example.

clue.text: Okay looking up somewhere to go or following Google Maps, say

indicators.note: in a down entry, looking upward means reading from bottom to top
to follow is to come after, so this part is placed second

blocks.note: Google Maps is an example of an app
the lav is the lavatory, a toilet
taken as written

explanation.surface: Is it all right to search for a place to visit, or to just follow the directions on Google Maps?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somewhere to go' sounds like a destination; it is the British slang lav, a loo. Okay is a noun here, as in 'give the okay'.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the okay means getting permission or a go-ahead, which is what approval is.

clue.text: Recall cars park outside, close to garage

indicators.note: being outside something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps another
the close of a word is its end, so only its last letter is taken

blocks.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a public park
Minis are small British cars
the final letter of garage

explanation.surface: A manufacturer's recall notice: cars are parked outside, near the garage.
explanation.walkthrough: Recall looks like a car maker summoning faulty vehicles back; it is the verb to remember. Rec, short for recreation ground, is British.
explanation.definitionFit: To reminisce is to look back fondly on and talk about past events, a way to remember them.

clue.text: Metal drawer

blocks.note: surface reading: a sliding metal compartment, as in a filing cabinet
setter's reading: something that draws, or attracts, metal towards it

explanation.walkthrough: Drawer, said as one syllable, is a box in a desk; split as draw-er it is a thing that pulls metal objects.
explanation.definitionFit: This object attracts iron and steel through its magnetic field, pulling such pieces in.

clue.text: Secretary for a broadsheet?

blocks.note: a PA is a personal assistant
per means for each, as in 'per day'

explanation.surface: Is a secretary needed to run a broadsheet newspaper?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks broadsheet as an example; broadsheets are the large-format serious British newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadsheet is a type of daily newspaper, and paper is the everyday short name for a newspaper.

clue.text: Forgive you what?

blocks.note: first meaning: to excuse an offence
second meaning: a request to repeat something not heard

explanation.walkthrough: 'You what?' is a blunt British way of asking someone to repeat themselves; the politer version is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works both as a verb for officially excusing an offence and as a polite request to repeat words.

clue.text: Back muscle stiff right away – using fingers

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the letters run right to left
with right sent away, the letter R is dropped

blocks.note: lats are the latissimus dorsi, the broad back muscles
stiff is rigid; R for right is taken out

explanation.surface: A back muscle is stiff, then straight away it is worked on by hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back muscle' reads as one anatomical phrase, and the lat is indeed a back muscle, but Back is also the order to read in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Digital in its older sense relates to the digits, the fingers, so it describes something done with fingers.

clue.text: Nameless benefactor gets access

indicators.note: without a name means the letter N standing for name is taken out

blocks.note: a donor is a benefactor

explanation.surface: An anonymous donor is allowed in to see something.
explanation.walkthrough: Nameless suggests an anonymous gift, which suits the benefactor; it removes N, the abbreviation for name.
explanation.definitionFit: A door is the way in to a room or building, so a means of entry.

clue.text: Comic actor working in animation

indicators.note: comic means funny or ridiculous, so these letters are played around with

blocks.note: taken as written
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A comedian has found work doing voices for an animated film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic actor' reads as a comedian, but Comic only tells you to rearrange the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartoon is a film made by animation, drawings photographed in sequence to create movement.

clue.text: See 5
In just seconds, conscientious objector declines class with daggers

indicators.note: taking only the seconds means keeping the second letter of each word

blocks.note: the second letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: A conscientious objector refuses within seconds to join a group carrying knives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In just seconds' sounds like a matter of time; it means second letters only.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeli are printers' dagger marks, used to flag footnotes or, beside a name, a person who has died.

clue.text: Explain worry about work European Union abandoned

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps round another
something abandoned is left behind, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: to eat someone is to worry them, as in 'what's eating you?'
labour is work; U for Union is dropped
E is the abbreviation for European
U is the abbreviation for Union; this is what is dropped

explanation.surface: Explain why you fret about your job now the EU has been left behind, a Brexit worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European Union' reads as the EU; the two words split, E staying at the end and U being removed from labour.
explanation.definitionFit: To elaborate is to explain something in more detail, expanding on a point with further information.
